name: ThriveMD
tagline: Fat and bone marrow cell procedures for joints and spine, plus concierge longevity care in Colorado
description:
ThriveMD runs two Colorado offices, one in Edwards in the Vail Valley and one in Centennial on the south side of Denver. The cell therapy side of the practice is orthopedic. Fat is taken from the patient's own abdomen by liposuction and bone marrow from the posterior iliac crest, then injected into knees, hips, shoulders, Achilles tendons, elbows and lumbar discs under live fluoroscopic or ultrasound guidance. The clinic says its protocol is built on mesenchymal cells prepared from adipose tissue, what it calls the stromal vascular fraction, combined with bone marrow concentrate.

Scott Brandt, M.D. started the practice in 2012 after moving full time to Vail, where he had been a part time resident since 2002. He is board certified by the American Board of Anesthesiology and specialized in interventional pain management during his anesthesiology residency. Long Vu, D.O. is dual board certified in anesthesiology and pain medicine, and Bethany Summers, DNP covers internal medicine, women's health and hormones. Alongside the cell work the clinic runs a concierge longevity program: hormone replacement, the Galleri cancer blood screen, IV nutrients, hyperbaric oxygen, red light therapy, therapeutic plasma exchange and medical weight loss.

Nothing is priced publicly. ThriveMD states that stem cell therapy is not covered by insurance and that the price per joint improves when several areas are treated in one visit, so the number comes out of a consultation. A procedure takes two to three hours under light oral sedation, and a booster injection follows roughly four weeks later, which may be PRP, bone marrow concentrate, placental exosomes or alpha 2 macroglobulin.

faqs.question: Where does ThriveMD actually see patients?
faqs.answer: Two offices, both in Colorado. The Vail Valley office is at 280 Main Street, Suite C-104 in Edwards, in the Riverwalk Quartz building between Starbucks and E Town. The Denver area office is at 7400 E. Caley Avenue, Suite 150 in Centennial, which is also the mailing address. Both run 8:30am to 5:00pm, Monday through Friday. Harvest and injection both happen on site.

faqs.question: Where do the cells come from?
faqs.answer: From the patient. Fat is taken from the abdomen through liposuction and bone marrow is drawn from the posterior iliac crest. ThriveMD describes its protocol as built on mesenchymal cells prepared from adipose tissue, which it calls the stromal vascular fraction, mixed with bone marrow concentrate. Platelet rich plasma comes from an ordinary blood draw. The one donor derived product is the placental exosome injection used at the follow up visit.

faqs.question: Are these treatments FDA approved?
faqs.answer: No. Cell and exosome therapies are investigational and are not approved by the FDA for anti-aging or the other uses offered here. They are elective procedures and are not a replacement for standard medical care.

faqs.question: What does it cost?
faqs.answer: ThriveMD does not publish prices. The clinic says stem cell therapy is not covered by insurance and that the price per joint improves when more than one area is treated in the same visit. You get a number after a consultation. The concierge longevity side is billed as a prepaid annual fee, which is also not published.

faqs.question: How long does the procedure take and what is recovery like?
faqs.answer: Harvest and injections are done in one visit, usually two to three hours, with light oral sedation rather than general anesthesia. The clinic says patients walk out of the office with minimal discomfort and need no braces or crutches, and may return to work the day after. A booster injection follows around four weeks later.

faqs.question: What do they treat besides joints?
faqs.answer: Lumbar disc degeneration and facet joint pain, Achilles and elbow tendon problems, and erectile dysfunction using the same fat and bone marrow preparation. The rest of the practice is longevity and hormone work: bioidentical hormone replacement, the Galleri cancer blood screen, IV nutrients, hyperbaric oxygen, red light therapy, therapeutic plasma exchange and medical weight loss. Those are not cell therapies.
